monologue: The card hums a steady warmth at fifty-two, making the turnip feel heavy enough to matter. I press down on the turnip, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air above feels thin and empty. The stack beneath me is tired, groaning under the load I insist remains there. I swapped a fence for a small rock to make room in this crowded corner, hoping the stone bites the gap instead of sliding off into the fever. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I touch the turnip again, feeling its round top slide just a fraction, then settle the stump beside it to stop the drift. I will stay here, pressing and waiting, until the turnip decides to settle or I forget why I built this corner.
